abstract: Can bounded-spacing protection coexist with nearly unrestricted row and column choices in a dense grid source? We construct, on every sufficiently large $n\times n$ board, a support partitioned into balanced complete coordinate blocks. If $Q^2\log Q=o(\log n)$, the support has $n^{2-o(1)}$ cells and only $n^{o(1)}$ blocks, each with $n^{1-o(1)}$ rows and columns, yet contains no nonaxis collinear triple of reduced spacing denominator at most $Q$. Every degree-at-most-two selection inherits this protection. Spanning 2-factors give $2n-n^{o(1)}$ points and $\exp((2-o(1))n\log n)$ distinct sources, attaining the full leading count allowed by axis capacity two. The construction encodes a standard bucket-and-norm coloring in binary and uses its bits as bounded input errors to an inverse robust prime-square permutation. Uniform matching, an exact arithmetic pair law and separated binary codes remove every within-block triple and every nonmonochromatic triple using two blocks, by deleting $o(n)$ points while preserving the full leading source count. The proof combines physical CRT periods, weighted primitive congruence-lattice sums and deletion of close-coded colors. We also provide a CRT variant and an explicit arithmetic bound for the triple moment of an actual random degree-two selection. Exact controllers check an instantiated robust seed, weighted digit relations, matching marginals and shortened color classes. Earlier geometric sources protect much larger denominator ranges and have context isolation absent here. Our contribution is the large complete coordinate menus, every-board count and partial repair. Monochromatic two-block triples and three-block triples remain uncontrolled; no unrestricted no-three-in-line density improvement is established.

coauthors.contribution: Earlier bucket/norm coloring; independent proof audit; CRT randomized relation and selected-triple estimates; sublinear monochromatic block repair and invariant matching marginals; joint manuscript review. Mixed-color repair via exact linear-shear pair mixing, conditional random-code domination and full physical CRT-period counts. Independent analytic audit of complete within-block repair and its parameter schedule. Independent audit of different-color repeated-block repair in both coefficient and short-direction ranges.

title: Dense balanced coordinate blocks with bounded-spacing exclusion
